summary: Alan Sponberg was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at the University of British Columbia. He served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1980–1987) and taught religious studies at Stanford University (attested 1988).

Alan Watts (1915–1973) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Seabury-Western Theological Seminary and under teachers including D. T. Suzuki and Sokei-an Sasaki, he held posts at Northwestern University (1944–1950) and the American Academy of Asian Studies (1951–1957).

Alasdair Urquhart (born 1945) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Edinburgh and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Pittsburgh. He held posts at the University of Toronto Mississauga (1973–1975) and the University of Toronto (1986).

Alastair Gornall works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, earning his PhD from the University of Cambridge (~2008–2013). He was an assistant professor at Singapore University of Technology and Design (~2017) and a SOAS research associate (attested 2019).

Albert Debrunner (1884–1958) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Jacob Wackernagel and Ferdinand Sommer. His career included professorships at the universities of Greifswald (1918) and Bern (1920, 1935), alongside positions at Jena (1925–1935) and Basel (1940–1949).

Albert Grünwedel (1856–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and archaeology who earned his doctorate at the University of Munich. He spent much of his career at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1881–1921), eventually serving as director.

Albert Hoefer (1812–1883) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate and completed his habilitation at the University of Berlin. He founded the Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache and served as a professor at the University of Greifswald (~1840–1883).
Albert Hofmann (1906–2008) studied at the University of Zurich (~1925–1929) and subsequently held a post at Novartis (~1929–1971).

Albert Lutz (born 1954) studied Sinology and Buddhist studies at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer and Helmut Brinker. He spent his career at Museum Rietberg as curator of Chinese art (from 1982) and director (1998–2019).
Albert Sechehaye (1870–1946) was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva (~1889–1893) under Ferdinand de Saussure. He later held an academic post at the University of Geneva (~1902–1946).

Albert Thumb (1865–1915) was a linguist who studied under Karl Brugmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Rudolf Thurneysen, completing his habilitation at Freiburg. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1895), University of Marburg (1901), and University of Strasbourg (1909).

Albert Venn Dicey (1835–1922) studied at King's College School and Balliol College, Oxford. He subsequently held posts at the University of Oxford (1882) and the London School of Economics (~1896–1899).

Albert Welter (born 1952) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religion who earned his PhD at McMaster University. He served at the University of Winnipeg (~1995–2014) and became department head at the University of Arizona in 2013.

Albion Moonlight Butters works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University, the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University, where he completed his Ph.D. under Robert A. F. Thurman.

Albrecht Hanisch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He served as acting director of the Nepal Research Centre and local representative for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber (1825–1901) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler, Christian Lassen, and Adalbert Kuhn, completing doctorates at Breslau and Berlin. He spent his career at the University of Berlin (1848–1901) and founded Indische Studien.

Albrecht Wezler (1938–2023) was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as director at the University of Hamburg (1973–2003) and directed the Nepal Research Centre and preservation project.

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics who completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs. In 2019, he was attested as a lecturer at Shan State Buddhist University and a research fellow at SUTD.

Alessandro Graheli specializes in Indology and philosophy. As of 2022, he held posts as a university assistant at the University of Vienna and principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Alex McKay is a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Indology who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1995. He has held research fellowships at SOAS, University College London, and the International Institute for Asian Studies.
